  its licence and licensor, and gives an explicit acceptance before download.
  A licence with conditions has its full text presented for agreement.
The acceptance is recorded as a receipt bound to the model digest.

- Every model Kilix fetches gets the OD-S treatment: an upstream source, a
  pinned digest where Kilix pins one, a first-use screen naming licence and
  licensor with agreement where conditions apply, and a digest-bound receipt
  under the OD-M/OD-U authority.

- A receipt covers the asset only while its binding is unchanged. The binding is the record
  digest, manifest digest, licence id, licence text digest, decision and licensor. Release and
  catalogue digests are recorded as acceptance context, not as coverage. A change to any
  binding field requires re-acceptance.

- Those records are the basis for the first-use licence screens of these four
  models. No new evidence packet or owner named determination is required for
  them.
- Recorded plainly: these are the only models whose first-use licence
  information rests on builder-authored records rather than an owner named
  determination.

- Distribution packages are installed by the user through their package manager,
  which carries the licence. Kilix records no receipt and gates nothing on them.
- When Kilix suggests an apt command for such a package, the message says the
  package is Debian non-free and that licence conditions apply.
- The mbrola-us1 evidence packet, already in progress, feeds that note's wording
  only. No owner determination is required for it.

Decision-class rule lives in the generator: affirmative iff the determined licence or a binding component or condition restricts use or redistribution (Apache-2.0, MIT, CC-BY-4.0, the Llama 3 Community License, Pocket TTS prohibited use); informational otherwise (Kristin public-domain statement); licensor always required.
